title: agentlake / quality
description: Cost and tokens per turn by prompt version, from agentlake.trace_events_rt. The eval-score panels are text, not charts, and stay that way: eval scores are rows in Postgres, not spans, and inventing a span type to make them chartable would be the fabrication this dashboard's own text refuses. See ADR-007 #6 and ADR-008.

panels.title: What these panels are, and where the eval numbers live

options.content:
**Live.** The two panels below run real SQL against `agentlake.trace_events_rt`, filtered on `attributes['prompt_version']`. `services/agent` stamps that on every AGENT_STEP and, via the `X-Prompt-Version` header, on every LLM_CALL -- which is the one that carries `cost_usd` and tokens, and therefore the only one these panels can divide (ADR-007 #6).

**Read them together with the eval.** A prompt that stops searching is *cheaper* per turn and *worse*: the ADR-008 v4-vs-v5 comparison shows exactly that. On cost alone this dashboard would recommend the worse prompt. That is not a flaw in the panels -- it is why quality is measured somewhere else and the two are read side by side.

**Eval scores are not here, and not because they are unfinished.** They live in `eval_runs` / `eval_results` in the metadata database, and Grafana here has only a ClickHouse datasource. Getting them onto this dashboard means a Trino datasource, not a new span type -- see the panels below.

panels.title: Cost per turn by prompt version
panels.description: trace_id is one turn (ADR-003 #4), so cost per turn is sum(cost_usd) over distinct trace_ids. Empty until something sets a prompt_version attribute.

targets.rawSql: SELECT $__timeInterval_ms(ts) AS time, attributes['prompt_version'] AS prompt_version, sum(cost_usd) / greatest(uniqExact(trace_id), 1) AS cost_per_turn_usd FROM agentlake.trace_events_rt WHERE $__timeFilter_ms(ts) AND attributes['prompt_version'] != '' GROUP BY time, prompt_version ORDER BY time

panels.title: Tokens per turn by prompt version

targets.rawSql: SELECT $__timeInterval_ms(ts) AS time, attributes['prompt_version'] AS prompt_version, (sum(prompt_tokens) + sum(completion_tokens)) / greatest(uniqExact(trace_id), 1) AS tokens_per_turn FROM agentlake.trace_events_rt WHERE $__timeFilter_ms(ts) AND attributes['prompt_version'] != '' GROUP BY time, prompt_version ORDER BY time

panels.title: Turn cost distribution (all traffic)
panels.description: The one panel here with data today: per-turn cost and step count across every trace, whether or not it carries a prompt_version. It is what the two panels above will look like once they have a dimension to split on.

targets.rawSql: SELECT trace_id, sum(cost_usd) AS cost_usd, sum(prompt_tokens) + sum(completion_tokens) AS tokens, uniqExact(span_id) AS spans, countIf(status != 'ok') AS errors FROM agentlake.trace_events_rt WHERE $__timeFilter_ms(ts) GROUP BY trace_id ORDER BY cost_usd DESC LIMIT 20

panels.title: Eval pass rate — measured, but not from ClickHouse

options.content:
### Measured in Postgres, not in spans

`make eval-ci` writes one `eval_results` row per graded example -- `hit_at_k`, `citation_ok`, `faithfulness`, `answer_quality` -- and an `eval_runs` row pinning the git sha, prompt version, corpus version and judge model that produced them.

**Why not a chart here.** A score is not a span. Emitting one as a span would need a new symbol in the Avro `EventType` enum, which the Flink reader schema would reject -- and stamping it on an `AGENT_STEP` would be labelling something that is not an agent step. Neither is worth doing to make a chart fit a datasource.

The published numbers are in `docs/eval/` and `eval/baseline.json`. Charting them needs a Trino datasource against `lake.analytics`, which is noted in ADR-008 and not built.

### The judge is validated, not just reported

Two rubric-anchored 1-5 scales per answer (`eval/rubric/`), graded by `claude-sonnet-5` through this platform's own gateway -- so judging is itself traced and costed, under `prompt_version = judge-v1`. **Judge spend shows up in the panels below as its own series**, which is deliberate: the cost of measuring quality is a cost.

A judge score is only worth reporting if someone has checked it tracks a human's. `make eval-label` emits a hand-labelling sheet -- without the judge's score on it, so it cannot anchor the labeller -- and `make eval-agreement` writes exact and within-1 agreement, plus Cohen's and quadratic-weighted kappa, to `docs/eval/agreement.md`, alongside a plain statement of what n=30 cannot establish.
